# Independent priority assessment — PR786 / 30001223

**Bounded conclusion: no complete published predecessor or published counterexample to the exact bridge was verified in this audit; priority remains inconclusive.** This does not establish firstness, novelty, or current worldwide openness. The verified mathematics may be reported as a counterexample to the broad printed formulation, with explicit credit for old component results. The original proof already disclaims novelty.

The exact reviewed source head is 34f21454986a28ca49f24999be3a0fd1b42755f8. The fixed result is: over an algebraically closed field of any odd characteristic p, at q=1, r=2p−1 and lambda=(2p−2,1), the Young module is simple while I_n(lambda) is nonprojective for every n>=2. The small p=3,lambda=(4,1) case is enough. The root math gate is closed; this audit assesses priority and source meaning, not a new math gate.

## What the primary report actually says

[Miyachi's OWR17/2009 contribution](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46217), printed944–947, defines the Schur-functor labels in §0.3. Conjecture7, printed946/PDF30, proposes the existential-rank projectivity bridge and then a stronger index-set version. The selected record's word “equivalently” is not justified by that formulation. Remark8 supplies the projective-to-simple-top direction. The characteristic-zero proviso below belongs to §0.5's rational-module method, after Conjecture7. It does not restrict the earlier broad assertion. The example addresses that broad assertion; it does not settle nontrivial quantum roots in characteristic zero.

Two actual copies were retrieved: current EMS SHA576e8b06155a4faf1d9118191265d4b99605bdd8f357c556ed55afe6aa1821d8, and TIB SHAe970ac8d0fc34f74b4c914a0aeab3502ad37b4b8e166150cbd979b3b87b51a95, the latter matching the original author's body pin. Printed946 was visually checked in both. They have different PDF bytes and extracted superscript order; no byte identity is claimed.

## Strong old-component overlap

The tiny example is not evidence for newly discovered local representation theory. [Turek–Wang2507.15505v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.15505), §3.1 p9, explicitly recalls the natural Specht module's simplicity when p does not divide the degree and cites James for Young-module structure. [Erdmann–Law2104.05317v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.05317), Prop3.1/Theorem3.3 pp5–6, supplies classical rank-two exact sequences and simplicity criteria; specializing p3 and restoring determinant produces the relevant nonsplit degree-five costandard. Their classical machinery points to Erdmann–Henke2002. The explicit specialization and convention checks appear in EXACT_COMPARISON.md.

[De Visscher–Donkin2005](https://openaccess.city.ac.uk/id/eprint/969/1/prinjjan12.pdf), actual manuscript printed7–13, supplies costandard reciprocity, injective/tilting equivalence for projective-injectives, and labelled rank truncation. Combined with the two possible dominating highest weights, these old facts yield the necessary every-rank obstruction. A general idempotent functor is not assumed to preserve projectivity. Their conditional Theorem5.1 is not imported unconditionally. Their separate projective-injective classification is not refuted by the negative Miyachi bridge.

These are substantial old ingredients and a short synthesis. I did not verify that an inspected source explicitly assembles them into this published counterexample, nor that a dated general theorem states the exact same negative bridge. “Follows from old machinery” and “previously published as this resolution” are different priority findings. Neither wording establishes a novel contribution.

## Adversarial exclusions and chronology

The author-hosted Elkin–Webb table for shape(4,1) is expressly in characteristic2 (November2020 PDF title/abstract, §5.5 pp10–11); it cannot be used as the characteristic3 example. Doty–Martin0708.2941v2 (11March2008) treats the degree-p hook block; the target has degree2p−1. Its Schur-functor discussion helps control signs, but degree-p results alone do not complete the target implication.

Ming Fang's ICRA21 slides, dated8August2024, treat Temperley–Lieb projective-injectives; slide9 mentions the DD classification as motivation. This is evidence of that source's scope, not a certificate that either problem remains globally open today. A fresh potentially relevant source, Koshitani–Sakurai2610.11276v1, was submitted8October2026 (internal date9October). Actual TheoremsA/B and §4 give general skew-bimodule reciprocity and examples. No Young/Schur specialization or exact target counterexample was found in the inspected body. Its abstract machinery is not a verified predecessor.

Labels and signs: the report defines Y^lambda=F I(lambda), using the stable-rank Schur functor. Its costandard Specht convention may dualize a usual Specht convention, which does not affect simplicity or the Young module's self-dual isomorphism type. Column p-regular means p-restricted, not row p-regular. The target (4,1) is row3-regular and not column3-regular. In Erdmann–Law, the numeral3 denotes weight difference, not the partition(3), degree3, or a finite GL2(F3) representation. Restoring determinant gives degree5. Finite GL2(F3) coincidences cannot replace rational GL2 labels.
